Next decisions — Solstice GXP baffle prototypes, P4

Decision scope: choose the next measurement or bench article that can retire a real uncertainty. The current alternatives are A (simple gated well), B (radial collector) and C (nested reservoir); their dimensions and counts are generated in CURRENT_DIMENSIONS.md. None has measured installed fit or demonstrated oil-control performance. The accepted P4 package and earlier releases are preserved separately in history with their original hashes. See INTERFACE_ASSESSMENT.md, TOLERANCE_SENSITIVITY.md, the source follow-up and QUALITY.md.

The smallest useful first evidence set

One matching removed pan with its original cover and pickup intact can answer most fit questions in one session. Record the actual pan/cover/fastener markings and photographs before disassembly. Include a scale in the same plane as each photographed feature. Photos alone do not measure hidden depths or thread engagement.

Establish a repeatable pan datum before measuring the cage: label all five cover mounting locations A1–A5 on one overview photo. Select three non-collinear, widely separated, repeatable contact points A1–A3, and define datum plane A through them, origin A1, +U along A1→A2, +N toward the cover, +V to complete a right-handed frame. Record exactly where each probe contacts. This construction does not assert that all five mounting seats are coplanar: record each seat normal, contact footprint and height residual, especially A4/A5. If the chosen points are not repeatably accessible, select another physical datum and document it; do not flatten the seats in CAD by assumption.

Record the transform from this datum to installed car forward/left/up and gravity, and subsequently to the current cage's X/Y/Z. The model's relieved −Y side has no established car direction. Preserve the original cover position and pickup/tube location. Measure the actual assembly rather than transferring a catalog photo's perspective.

The fit session needs these together:

  1. All five seat/contact locations, bolt seating surfaces, original clamp stack, fastener identity, under-head length, threaded segment, usable boss depth and actual engagement without bottoming. Record cover seating before any added strap. A partially threaded or thread-forming screw cannot be replaced on the strength of an M6 label alone.
  2. Registered cavity/floor sections and cast obstacles across the intended cage footprint, not just maximum width/depth. Record the cover underside/relief, pickup screen/tube and drain route in the same datum. Include local protrusions and the lowest cover areas over each door sweep. A large overall pan envelope cannot close these measurements.
  3. Uncertainty and method for every observation: instrument, resolution, calibration/reference check, repeat readings, datum repeatability and access limits. Instrument resolution alone is not measurement uncertainty. Retain raw measurements and photographs under research/ with traceable filenames, then enter evidence paths and uncertainty in MEASUREMENTS_REQUIRED.csv.
  4. A complete disposable trial assembly of the candidate envelope, with representative mount, pin-head, weld and purchased-hardware envelopes. Use it only after the measurements establish a plausible location. Check cover seating, independent gate travel, pickup clearance, floor/bypass gaps, insertion/removal and tool access. A single hinge coupon cannot answer full-cage fit.

No fixed minimum pan, pickup, floor or thread-engagement clearance is assigned without applicable evidence and the actual configuration. The dimensional comparison must include measurement uncertainty, process error, temperature and load allowance before a release criterion is chosen.

MEASUREMENT_PRIORITY.csv maps every one of the 29 existing unknown worksheet items to these ranks. Ranks are dependency/decision priorities, not estimates of safety or test effort. Ranks can overlap: stock and pin traceability must precede the A hinge coupon. Coupon work can proceed independently of pan measurement, but its result does not close ranks 1–4. If a purchased-door alternative is reconsidered later, verify its exact supplier revision and mounting method before treating it as a current option.

Choose among the three with the same conditions

Keep the unmodified OEM system as a fourth comparison baseline. A has the simplest current gated layout and fewest custom gate locations; refill and directional retention still need evidence. B adds diagonal collection, more seams and guide-vane access questions. C adds a second gate stage and the largest nested assembly; staged buffering is a hypothesis and serial gates may restrict refill. All three use the shared custom hinge family, so joining, alignment, thin-leaf distortion, pin heading and fatigue need qualification. No current variant is preferred on performance evidence.

A variant becomes the next fitted prototype when its measured envelope and attachment are feasible and its specific mechanism/process trial is credible. Select the final architecture only after common-condition refill/retention evidence and the physical holds in QUALITY.md are addressed. Record why alternatives were rejected using actual measurements, not the number of doors or how the render looks.

Quantities to record in the decisive bench comparison

Use the same oil specification, measured temperature, orientation/effective-gravity scenario, initial inventory and fixture geometry for each comparison. Identify fixture leakage separately. Record upstream/downstream levels, differential head, door angle/initiation/recovery, time-resolved supplied/drained volume, trapped air, residual oil and repeatability. Run the stock baseline through the same observable conditions. State which real operating conditions the fixture cannot reproduce.

If level measurements have uncertainties u1 and u2, a conservative differential-head uncertainty is u1+u2 unless a justified correlated model is available. Compare an opening-initiation head with the measured available refill-head range and uncertainty; do not adopt an arbitrary universal opening-head target. Similarly, a simple chamber balance dV/dt = Q_in − Q_pickup − Q_out is a bookkeeping check only after those flows and usable inventory are established. Window area, floor-gap area and enclosed geometric volume alone do not predict those flows or starvation time.

Before each physical test, record the named revision, method, observable pass/fail question, justified loads/conditions and stop criteria. Use the coupon results template as a template and retain raw repeats in a separate evidence file. No physical test has been performed in this project packet.
